description: The speaker introduces herself in the transcript as “Donna,” while the supplied metadata gives “Danna”; her surname is listed in the metadata as Arrieta Ventura. In this UCF Remembers 9/11 recording, dated September 11, 2026, she reflects on family connections to the September 11, 2001 attacks and their aftermath. She recounts that her mother, an immigrant from Peru, was studying in high school in New York in 2001 and could communicate with family in Huánuco only every week or two. The speaker relays her great-aunt’s account of listening to radio coverage in Lima and fearing for the mother while communication was unavailable. She also recounts a story from her middle-school science teacher about his friend, who worked at or near the World Trade Center and was surrounded and hidden by coworkers and friends while walking in New York in the weeks after the attacks. The account emphasizes fear and the attacks’ cultural effects in the United States and internationally, including in rural areas.
